open_questions: Centroid on_target not measured; on-target confirmation with higher S/N photometry or spectroscopy would rule out a very close blend.
High eccentricity indicated by fit_log_density_ratio=-1.452 and star_density_penalty=49.76; RV mass measurement needed to determine density and confirm planetary mass.
dossier.public_summary: A 1.7% deep, flat-bottomed dip recurs every 12.9 days on a nearby 0.25-solar-radius M dwarf with no odd-even difference or secondary eclipse. Its size implies a ~3.5 Earth-radius planet, and no nearby stars within a TESS pixel can produce it. The long transit and puzzling density suggest the orbit may be eccentric, but a planet remains the best explanation pending mass measurement.

reasons.why: Strongly flat-bottomed transit shape favours a planetary transit over a grazing stellar eclipse or V-shaped blend.
Radius 3.5 Rearth on a 0.248 Rsun M dwarf is well below the stellar regime, well supported size for a planet despite needing no binarity.
No odd/even depth difference and no significant secondary (secondary.snr=2.793 <5) despite uniform sector depths, arguing against an EB at twice the period.
Centroid is inconclusive with no clear difference image, but neighbours.plausible_within_1px=0 and closest_that_could=45.9 arcsec with contratio=0.001564 makes a blended neighbour eclipse unlikely.
Duration ratio 1.425 with fit_b=0.7609 shows a long but still acceptable transit for this very small star, not an implausibly large EB.
